learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Moves in 4 directions or 8? (4.)
- Can walls block everything? (Yes → −1.)
- Grid size? (Up to 1000 × 1000 — one BFS, not one per cell.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: Running BFS from every cell is O(cells²). Running it from every supply point at once is one BFS: the first time the wave reaches a cell, that is its nearest supply.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "P."ut every supply point in the BFS queue at distance 0 before starting, so one breadth-first pass gives every cell its distance to the nearest supply in O(rows × cols)."

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe put every supply point in the BFS queue at distance 0 before starting, so one breadth-first pass gives every cell its distance to the nearest supply in O(rows × cols). Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Distances concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."
- *Requirement change* — "The requirement changed: Add Supply.WorstCase(grid): the largest distance of any reachable cell (0 if none). List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- BFS from each cell (or each supply) separately.
- DFS — it does not give shortest distances.
- Marking visited on dequeue instead of enqueue (cells queued many times).
